subject: Post-demo: canonical prompts, measurement definitions, and acceptance criteria

Subject: Thanks for the demo — next on SLO/benchmark details

Hi Rishi,

Thanks for the demo this morning — the team found the streaming examples helpful. As discussed, we want a concise spec we can run with our infra team to validate the latency and concurrency claims. High level asks from our side:
- End-to-end p95 latency for a 512-token response under normal traffic (target <= 220ms)
- Sustained throughput at 250 concurrent users (observed RPS target >= 180)
- Streaming token latency (first-byte within 75ms, per-token steady-state < 30ms)
- A reproducible harness so our QA can run the same prompt bundle and seed settings

Can you send a minimal prompt set + measurement definitions and a simple runbook we can hand to their infra/QA? Also, we'll need a short list of the exact model binary/quantization profile you used in the demo.

— Sophie
Sophie Turner
Head of ML Engineering, Acme Retail

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 2 Aug 2028 12:42:00 -07:00
Subject: Internal: draft harness + measurement notes for ACME

Quick internal draft before we share: summary of measurement definitions and reproducibility notes. Please skim and flag anything we should not share verbatim.

- Measurement windows:
  * Cold-run: container start, empty KV cache, N=5 runs per prompt, collect first-byte and end-to-end timing.
  * Warm-run: after prefix caching and 10 warmup requests, N=50 runs spread over 10 minutes.
- Latency definitions:
  * First-byte latency (streaming): time from request POST to first SSE chunk received by client. Measured per request.
  * End-to-end p95: time from POST to final chunk (or final token) received; report p50/p95/p99 and median throughput.
- Throughput/concurrency shaping:
  * Use a closed-loop runner (locust/vegeta style) to prescribe 250 concurrent virtual users; measure steady-state RPS over a 5-minute window after warmup.
- Reproducibility knobs:
  * Fixed model_version tag (e.g., redwood-open-v2-13b:r2.4-opt).
  * Deterministic prompt seeds where applicable (for sampling-free evals); for stochastic sampling, fix random seeds and sample counts.
  * Hardware spec: list GPU type, driver, CUDA/cuDNN versions and kernel flags.
- Acceptance criteria (proposal):
  * p95 latency <= 220ms (end-to-end) for 512-token median responses
  * streaming first-byte <= 75ms; per-token steady-state <= 30ms
  * steady-state throughput >= 180 RPS at 250 concurrent users
  * qualitative: no >1% error-rate (5xx or timeouts) during steady-state window

I'll attach the candidate prompt bundle and the harness spec to the outbound mail. If you think the p95 target is aggressive we can add a tiered acceptance (gold/silver) to reflect quantized vs FP16 configs.

- Marissa
Principal Perf Engineer, Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Post-demo: canonical prompts, measurement definitions, and acceptance criteria

Great — appreciate the quick turnaround. Short answers and next steps: 

1) Instrumentation: client-observed SSE chunk arrival is preferred for acceptance results. We'll include an optional nginx/proxy timing snippet in the harness so you can compare client vs proxy numbers. The harness writes both timings to the CSV output (client_first_byte_ms, proxy_first_byte_ms).

2) Top-10 for smoke: we flagged prompts 1-10 in acme_canonical_prompts_v1.txt with a BUYER_FLOW or PERSONALIZATION tag. Start with those for the Monday session.

3) Prefix caching: yes — demo used per-session prefix caching for personalization keys. For the harness, we provide two modes: caching_enabled=true (to match demo) and caching_enabled=false (to measure worst-case). Please run both; our acceptance criteria above assume caching_enabled=true.

Attached to this thread: acme_canonical_prompts_v1.txt (30 prompts, top10 flagged), eval-harness-spec-20280802.md, harness-run.sh, Dockerfile.harness

Proposed Monday session (2028-08-06 09:30 PST): 60 minutes to run the warm-run targets, collect CSV artifacts, and review p95/p99 and error rates together. Ben will join to advise on tuning autoscaling if observed throughput is below target.

If that time works, I'll send a calendar invite and a temporary access token for the demo config so you can validate the model tag.

Best,
Rishi
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
